chapter: Opinions, Edgar Battle and closing stories
title: Rock and younger drummers: paying dues

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Let's just maybe deal a little bit with let's say music that's come about in the last 20 years, such as rock and some of the more recent drummers, say somebody like Elvin Jones or people who have come around after him.
What do you think about ... like that?

Well as far as the music is concerned, I've always said there is some good rock and there's some bad rock. The same way when the swing or the be-bop era was in, there was some good be-bop and there was some bad and that goes the same way with the music. Now as far as these drummers are concerned, there's Elvin Jones has got a very nice name, he happens to be one of the good ones. Some drummers that try to play like Elvin is very bad, they sound bad. And I would say that it runs in cycles like that. If you're good, you can play 'Home Sweet Home' so it sounds good. Sometimes you may be able to play Home Sweet Home and it'll sound bad, and drummers that try to play like Buddy Rich all of a sudden. Well they forget that Buddy Rich came up in that old school way back there with Joe Marsala, Artie Shaw, and they forget about Elvin Jones way back there with these other little bands. I think he was with, oh goodness, a lot of them little swing bands before he even started playing this.
Alvin used to play, I guess....
Sweets Edison, and yeah, see, so he's got all that background in back of him. See so many guys try to — trumpet players try to play like Diz. Well Diz was way back

there with Fletcher Henderson, Jay McShann, Billy Eckstein, Cab Calloway. He's got all that footage underneath him. You know that kind of background. So Dizzy knows where it's at. A lot of these kids will try to start where Dizzy's at now and they don't know where it's at.
They get a few cliches under their fingers, but they really don't know what he's doing... or for that matter sax players who try to play like Coltrane.

Impossible, see 'cause Coltrane came up in that school, you know, good foundation, working with those bands, different bands, different style bands, and they try to pick up right where Coltrane is now before he died, or the same way with the drummers, try to play like Max or Roy Haynes or Elvin or Buddy, and you just can't you know, it's impossible to be made a doctor over night. There's no way in the world that I've said it over and over, that you can skip grade school and go to high school. See, you've got to pay those dues first, and find out where it's at and then from there on you can build and just build.
